name: South Africa
note: South African estate administration, curatorship and health decision-making: Administration of Estates Act 66 of 1965, Intestate Succession Act 81 of 1987 and Wills Act 7 of 1953 from the Department of Justice, with the National Health Act 61 of 2003 and Mental Health Care Act 17 of 2002 from the Government Printer. There is no enduring power of attorney: a power of attorney is common law and lapses on the grantor’s incapacity, so the written health mandate under National Health Act s 7 is the only advance appointment recorded here. Two statutory routes run in parallel for property — curatorship under the Administration of Estates Act and an administrator under the Mental Health Care Act. The Mental Health Care Act citations carry no quote because the Government Printer’s scan has a damaged text layer; the sections were read but are not reproduced verbatim.

roles.name: Curator (letters of curatorship)
roles.summary: South Africa’s statutory substitute decision maker for property. Nobody may administer another’s property as curator without letters of curatorship from the Master, and the letters themselves fix the authority — a single act, care of the property, full administration, or carrying on a business.

assigned.event: Curator nominated by will or written instrument, or the Master appoints one where there is no nomination, where an absentee owns property, or where a court could appoint

starts.event: On letters of curatorship being granted by the Master; without them no one may take care of or administer the property

ends.event: Removal from office, the removal provisions for executors applying to curators
Death of the person, when the estate passes to the executor

states.label: Letters granted; authority as the letters specify

transitions.event: Curator nominated by will or written instrument (s 72)
Master appoints where there is no nomination, or for an absentee’s property (s 73)
Letters of curatorship granted; the letters fix whether the curator may perform a particular act, take care of, administer, or carry on a business (ss 71, 76)
Removal from office, s 54 applying to curators through s 85
Death of the person; the estate passes to the executor (s 14)

roles.name: Executor testamentary
roles.summary: An executor nominated by will. Authority comes from the Master of the High Court issuing letters of executorship on written application, not from the will alone.

assigned.event: Nominated as executor by a will that has been registered and accepted in the office of the Master

starts.event: Master issues letters of executorship on written application

transitions.event: Nomination by a valid will (Wills Act s 2)
Master issues letters of executorship (s 14)
conditions: will registered and accepted by the Master

transitions.event: Estate liquidated and distributed

roles.name: Executor dative
roles.summary: Where nobody was nominated by will, or the nominee cannot be found or will not act, the Master appoints. On intestacy the estate then devolves under the Intestate Succession Act.

assigned.event: Master acts where there is no nomination, or the nominee's whereabouts are unknown, or they have died, are incapacitated or refuse to act

ends.event: Estate liquidated and distributed to those entitled

transitions.event: Master appoints on failure of nomination (s 18(1))
Distribution, on intestacy under the Intestate Succession Act s 1

roles.name: Estate dealt with without an executor
roles.summary: Where the estate is below the amount the Minister sets by notice in the Gazette, the Master may dispense with an executor altogether and direct how the estate is to be liquidated and distributed.

assigned.event: Master decides the estate falls under the Gazetted amount

starts.event: Master gives directions in place of appointing an executor

ends.event: Estate liquidated and distributed as directed

transitions.event: Master dispenses with an executor (s 18(3))
conditions: estate does not exceed the amount determined by the Minister by notice in the Gazette

transitions.event: Estate liquidated and distributed as directed

roles.name: Person mandated in writing to consent
roles.summary: South Africa has no enduring power of attorney, but the National Health Act lets a user mandate someone in writing to give informed consent to health services on their behalf once the user cannot give it themselves.

assigned.event: User mandates a person in writing to grant consent on his or her behalf

starts.event: When the user is unable to give informed consent

transitions.event: User mandates a person in writing to grant consent (s 7(1)(a)(i))
User becomes unable to give informed consent (s 7(1))
Death of the user; the estate passes to the executor (Administration of Estates Act s 14)

roles.name: Statutory consent order (spouse, partner, parent, grandparent, adult child, sibling)
localNames: in the specific order as listed
roles.summary: Where the user cannot consent and nobody has been mandated or authorised, the Act names who consents, in a fixed order: spouse or partner, then a parent, grandparent, adult child, brother or sister.

assigned.event: No person mandated in writing or authorised by law or court order, and the user cannot give informed consent

starts.event: Consent is given by the spouse or partner, or failing them a parent, grandparent, adult child, brother or sister, in the specific order listed

transitions.event: User unable to consent and nobody mandated or authorised, so the statutory order applies (s 7(1)(b))
Death of the user (Administration of Estates Act s 14)

roles.name: Donor of body or tissue, or the family in the statutory order
localNames: donation of human bodies and tissue
roles.summary: A person competent to make a will may donate their body or specified tissue by will, by a document signed before two competent witnesses, or by an oral statement before two. The donation must name a donee or it is null and void. Absent a donation or a contrary direction, the family may donate in a fixed order.

assigned.event: Person competent to make a will donates the body or specified tissue by will, signed document before two witnesses, or oral statement before two witnesses

starts.event: After the person’s death; the donation must have nominated a donee or it is null and void

ends.event: Donation acted on, or the family donate in the statutory order where the deceased made none

states.label: Donation null and void, no donee nominated
Family may donate in the statutory order

transitions.event: Donation by will, signed document before two witnesses, or oral statement before two (s 62(1)(a))
Donation made but no donee nominated, so it is null and void (s 62(1)(b)-(c))
No donation and no contrary direction given while alive (s 62(2))
Death; the nominated donee may act on the donation (s 62(1))
Spouse, partner, major child, parent, guardian, major brother or major sister donate, in the specific order (s 62(2))

roles.name: Administrator of property (Mental Health Care Act)
roles.summary: The modern route for property, running alongside curatorship under the Administration of Estates Act. A Master of a High Court appoints an administrator to care for and administer the property of a mentally ill person or a person with severe or profound intellectual disability.

assigned.event: Any person over 18 applies in writing, under oath or solemn affirmation, to a Master of a High Court, or a High Court orders an appointment after an appeal or enquiry

starts.event: The Master appoints an administrator to care for and administer the property

ends.event: Term of office terminated on application by the person concerned, the administrator, or whoever applied for the appointment
Death of the person, when the estate passes to the executor

states.label: Application to the Master, or High Court order

transitions.event: Application in writing under oath to a Master of a High Court, or a High Court order after appeal or enquiry (ss 59, 60)
Master appoints an administrator to care for and administer the property (s 59)
Term of office terminated on application by the person, the administrator, or the original applicant (s 64)
Death of the person (Administration of Estates Act s 14)

probateGrantName.note: Issued by the Master of the High Court rather than a court, both where an executor is nominated by will and where the Master appoints.

smallEstateWithoutGrant.note: The Master may dispense with an executor where the estate does not exceed an amount the Minister sets by notice in the Gazette. The Act itself does not state a figure, and the current notice was not retrieved, so no amount is recorded here.

healthAgentStartsOn.note: The mandate operates when the user is unable to give informed consent; there is no registration or court step.

organDonationModel.note: A donation must be made by will, by signed document before two competent witnesses, or orally before two, and must nominate a donee or it is null and void. Absent a donation, the family may donate in the order the Act sets.
